title: Denmark | RSF
body: The subsidy system provides most of the funding to the public broadcasters, the rest being allocated to privately-owned media. The money is distributed by public institutions according to a principle of independence. Due to the country’s size, it is still possible to get government funds to support small printed media and specialised magazines.

title: Media Policy and Independence in Denmark - European Journalism Observatory - EJO
body: April 7, 2012 - The media market in Denmark is unique due to its small size, which creates a fragile system that relies on both privatization and publically funded subsidies. At the core of the system is the shared need to keep the media both pluralistic and independent, which is becoming gradually more difficult in the digital age.

title: Denmark - Centre for Media Pluralism and Media Freedom
body: June 27, 2025 - While Denmark currently operates under a well-functioning, trust-based system that safeguards media independence, such a system remains vulnerable in exceptional circumstances, such as crises.
